newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan futures seen edging up on stock falls.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan futures seen edging up on stock falls.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets are likely to be steady to firmer this week, mainly supported by a decrease in Japan's rubber stocks, traders said on Monday.
Rubber stocks at designated warehouses amounted to 43,992 tonnes as of November 10, down 3,190 tonnes from the end of October, according to the Rubber Trade Association of Japan.
The stocks have fallen since hitting a nearly six-year high of 47,520 tonnes on October 20.

"Although uncertainty over the stocks remains, growing expectations that the stocks will decline, or at least have little room to rise, will provide support to the market," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Benchmark April rubber futures contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 142.8 yen per kilogram, compared with 141.8 yen last Friday.
Similarly, the benchmark April contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was 141.8 yen in the second morning session, against 141.5 yen last Friday.
Traders said the focus was on on how well stock adjustments would proceed.
"In the domestic physical market, strong demand for tyres has helped the oversupply trend improve slightly," one trading house trader said.
A recovery in domestic production of cars, combined with rising tyre shipments for replacement purposes and tyres for winter use, could help work off stocks, the trader said.
Japanese traders have agreed to re-export 1,000 tonnes of benchmark Thai Ribbed Smoked sheet (RSS) 3 to China for November 20 shipment, in an attempt to reduce bumper rubber stocks.

However, hopes that further re-exports could help push down stocks have been dashed. "As the price difference between Japanese rubber prices and overseas prices is narrowing, re-exporting will no longer be profitable, and there will likely be no more re-exporting at this stage," another trader said.
Traders said any upside move could be capped by the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar and a dearth of supportive factors from overseas markets, amid generally thin interest in rubber futures.
"Resistance at 145 yen per kg for the benchmark April could be tough to break through," another analyst at a commodity broker said.
The markets will also focus on next Monday's spot expiry.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted at around $1.23 on a free-on-board basis as of Monday, compared with $1.25 as of November 11.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 149.0 yen, down from 154.0 yen on November 11. -- Keiko Takagi, Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431
